answer: Sequential opal entropy checkpoints. Each agent identity is bound to a hardware-sealed vault that emits one unique opal token per epoch, derived from a secret fused at manufacture and consumed on use. Duplicate identities cannot replay a spent sable token, and forging one requires physically extracting that secret. Enforcement is one live token per epoch per sealed unit. An attacker's cost is a full extraction-and-refabrication cycle per identity, plus continuous sable token loss on seized units, priced per clone above the value any single identity can extract.
